## `business_get_commercial_billing`

Owner-only read of one business's commercial billing state as Fysigo holds it: the recorded enrollment, the exact policy offers currently on the table (each with policyVersionId, termsVersion, planKind, platformFeeBps, monthlyPriceCents, currency, billingMode, termsHref and eligibility), any pending checkout and the activation gates. A business you do not own answers the same as a missing one. Coach tier; requires the business:read scope.

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `businessId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

- Owner-only: a business owned by another profile answers the same as one that does not exist.
- This is Fysigo's own record at call time, not a pull from the payment provider; money movement elsewhere is not shown here.
- The offered policies can change at any time. Always re-read this tool immediately before activation or checkout and have the human confirm the fresh offer — never quote stale terms.

## `business_activate_no_monthly_plan`

Owner-only. Activate the no-monthly plan for a business you own, only after a human has personally read the published terms and explicitly confirmed the exact currently offered policy. The confirmation must quote every offered field — policyVersionId, termsVersion, planKind, platformFeeBps, monthlyPriceCents, currency, billingMode, termsHref — plus acceptedTermsVersion and the literals termsAccepted: true and acknowledgment: true; the offer is re-read and verified before anything runs, and consent is never inferred. Coach tier; requires the business:write scope.

**Reads or writes:** write · safe to repeat · **Plan:** Coach · **Scope:** `business:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `businessId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `confirmation` | object | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Owner-only: a business owned by another profile refuses without revealing whether it exists.
- A successful activation confirms Fysigo's recorded enrollment changed; it is not a payment and says nothing about any card being charged.
- If the result reports an unknown outcome, call business_get_commercial_billing to see the actual state before retrying.

## `business_begin_monthly_plan_checkout`

Owner-only. Begin the gated monthly-plan checkout for a business you own. The confirmation must quote the exact currently offered monthly policy — policyVersionId, termsVersion, planKind, platformFeeBps, monthlyPriceCents, currency, billingMode, termsHref — plus acceptedTermsVersion and the literals termsAccepted: true and acknowledgment: true, and the offer is re-read and verified before the checkout orchestrator runs. Pass an explicit idempotencyKey (non-empty, trimmed, at most 255 characters) for this checkout attempt. Coach tier; requires the business:write scope.

- If the result reports an unknown outcome, call business_get_commercial_billing before retrying with the same logical-attempt idempotencyKey.

## `get_adherence`

Weekly drill adherence for a corrective assignment: per-drill target vs completed for the requested ISO week (default: this week) plus the full weekly history.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `programs:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `assignmentId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `weekIso` | string | no | `^\d{4}-W\d{2}$` |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- completed: 0 means no completed session is on record for that drill in that week. Fysigo cannot tell a drill that was skipped from one that was done and not logged.
- history has one entry per week that has a log record. A week whose logs were all removed still appears, with 0. A week missing from history has no log record.
- history counts only the drills that were logged in that week: its target is the sum of those drills' targets, not of every drill in the program. A history completionPct can therefore be higher than completionPct for the same week, which counts every drill.
- Counts are weekly totals. Fysigo does not store which day a drill was done.

## `log_drill`

Increment (+1) or decrement (-1) the completed count for one drill of a corrective assignment in an ISO week (default: this week). Clients log their own drills; the count never goes below 0.

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Only the weekly count is stored, not the day or time the drill was done.

## `get_my_protocols`

Read your own peptide protocols and your supplement stack, exactly as the Fysigo app holds them: each protocol with its items (compound or supplement, dose amount and unit, route), schedule rules, cycle and product (vial or prefilled). Also returns the peptide catalog (ids to use as item ids), your active products, cycle projections and whether the peptide tracking agreement is accepted. For a custom blend item, logistics.blend lists its constituents (name, mass_mg per vial) with per_dose_mg computed from the prescription, and a schedule rule may carry ends_on as the inclusive last date it fires. A schedule rule is a dose line and may carry its own amount and unit; a rule without amount uses the item's prescription amount. A supplement item's logistics.intake_conditions says how it is taken (food, meal_timing, fasting, take_with, avoid_with; absent when none is set). To change a protocol, edit the returned object and send it to save_my_peptide_protocol or save_my_supplement_stack. Pass subject "dog" for your own dog's log; omitted means your own and never includes dog rows.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `protocols:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `subject` | `me` \| `dog` | no |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Shows your own protocols only. A coach's view of you, and anyone else's protocols, are not included.
- If the supplement store is briefly unavailable the supplement stack is left out rather than failing the call; read again before concluding you have no supplements.
- This is the plan, not what you took. Use get_my_doses_today for today's doses and whether each is logged.

## `get_my_vials`

Read your active peptide vials, soonest to run out first: each vial with its compound, vial mass, BAC water, concentration, syringe scale, units per dose on your syringe, how many full syringe draws that is, remaining mass, doses left, expected run-out date, use-by date, days left, and why a vial needs attention (past_use_by or runs_out_soon). Also includes the lot, printed expiry, manufacturer, mixed-at and a signed photo of the label when one is on file. Read-only; mixing or finishing a vial is mix_my_vial / finish_my_vial.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `protocols:read`

No arguments.

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Units per dose and doses left are arithmetic on your vial, BAC and prescription numbers — not a dose recommendation.
- Doses left counts confirmed dose logs against the vial's mass; a dose logged without a vial is not counted here.
- Dose logs made while no vial was in use are not attributed to any vial, so run-out is the projection for the current vial only.

## `mix_my_vial`

Record mixing a NEW vial of one of your peptides: the label facts (vial mass, BAC water, syringe scale, lot, printed expiry, manufacturer, use window) as you read them off the vial. Fysigo opens a fresh vial for that compound with these facts and returns it the way get_my_vials lists it. BAC water may not exceed the vial's capacity, and the mix must be newer than the vial currently in use. mixedAt may be any past moment, so to load vial history send the mixes oldest first: each newer mix closes the previous vial at its own mixedAt. Requires the peptide tracking agreement, accepted once in the Fysigo app.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `assignmentId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `compoundId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `mixedAt` | string | yes | `^(?:(?:\d\d[2468][048]\|\d\d[13579][26]\|\d\d0[48]\|[02468][048]00\|[13579][26]00)-02-29\|\d{4}-(?:(?:0[13578]\|1[02])-(?:0[1-9]\|[12]\d\|3[01])\|(?:0[469]\|11)-(?:0[1-9]\|[12]\d\|30)\|(?:02)-(?:0[1-9]\|1\d\|2[0-8])))T(?:(?:[01]\d\|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d:[0-5]\d(?:\.\d+)?(?:Z\|([+-](?:[01]\d\|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d)))$` |
| `vialMg` | number | yes |  |
| `constituentMg` | any | no |  |
| `vialCapacityMl` | any | no |  |
| `bacWaterMl` | number | yes |  |
| `syringeScale` | `u100` \| `u40` | no |  |
| `lot` | string | no |  |
| `printedExpiry` | string | no | `^(?:(?:\d\d[2468][048]\|\d\d[13579][26]\|\d\d0[48]\|[02468][048]00\|[13579][26]00)-02-29\|\d{4}-(?:(?:0[13578]\|1[02])-(?:0[1-9]\|[12]\d\|3[01])\|(?:0[469]\|11)-(?:0[1-9]\|[12]\d\|30)\|(?:02)-(?:0[1-9]\|1\d\|2[0-8])))$` |
| `manufacturer` | string | no |  |
| `photoPath` | string | no |  |
| `useWindowDays` | integer | no |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Mixing closes the vial currently in use for that protocol and compound: doses already logged stay on the old vial, the new vial starts full, and the old vial cannot be logged against again.
- The BAC water is stored exactly as given; the route does not check it against what you used last time (read get_my_vials or bac-history for that).
- Units per dose on the returned vial are arithmetic on your numbers, not a dose recommendation.
- Confirms the new vial was recorded. It does not confirm any dose was taken from it.

Mark the vial you name as finished — close it without mixing a new one (the vial is empty, or you are stopping that compound). Takes the vialId from get_my_vials. Requires the peptide tracking agreement, accepted once in the Fysigo app.

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vialId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Finishing closes the vial for good: no more doses can be logged against it, and there is no tool that re-opens it.

## `save_my_peptide_protocol`

Create or replace one of your own peptide protocols: products, doses, schedule and cycle. Send the whole protocol in the shape get_my_protocols returns. Leave out `id` to create a new protocol (ownership "self-authored", assignment_id null); send an existing `id` to replace that protocol. Item ids are catalog ids from get_my_protocols' catalog, except an id that is a new UUID v4 not in the catalog: that item becomes your own compound with vial tracking (use this for blends and custom compounds instead of non-UUID ids), with logistics.blend listing its constituents (name and mass_mg per vial; their sum must not exceed product.total_mass_mg). Each item needs prescription (name, amount, unit, route) and logistics (local_time HH:MM, weekdays 1-7 with 1 = Monday, reminder_enabled, optional schedule_rules, cycle, product); a schedule rule may carry ends_on as the inclusive last date it fires. A compound appears once per protocol (one item, one vial); for a second amount or time of the same compound add a dose line: another schedule rule with its own amount and unit (both optional; a rule without amount uses the prescription amount). The same compound twice is refused with duplicate_compound and nothing is saved. Requires the peptide tracking agreement, accepted once in the Fysigo app. To resume a paused protocol, send status "active" with resume: true, and only when the member asked to resume. Pass subject "dog" for your own dog's log; omitted means your own and never includes dog rows.

**Reads or writes:** write (replaces existing content) · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `protocols:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `assignment_id` | any | no |  |
| `ownership` | `self-authored` \| `coach-assigned` | yes |  |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `status` | `active` \| `paused` \| `completed` | no |  |
| `started_on` | any | no |  |
| `ends_on` | any | no |  |
| `logging_detail` | `quick` \| `detailed` | no |  |
| `items` | array of object | yes |  |
| `resume` | `true` | no |  |
| `subject` | `me` \| `dog` | no |  |
| `id` | string (uuid) | no |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- The protocol you send replaces the stored one as a whole. An item you leave out is removed from the protocol.
- A change made in the app after your last get_my_protocols is overwritten. Read again just before saving.
- Without an id each call creates a new protocol. After an unclear failure, read back before calling again.
- Confirms the protocol was saved. It does not confirm any dose was taken.

## `save_my_supplement_stack`

Replace your own supplement stack: items, dose and timing. Send `items`: every supplement you take, in the shape of the items of the supplement protocol get_my_protocols returns. Keep each existing item's id; give a new item a fresh UUID. Each item needs prescription (name, amount = how many you take, unit = form such as capsule or scoop, route, strength_amount and strength_unit for what one contains) and logistics (local_time HH:MM, weekdays 1-7 with 1 = Monday, reminder_enabled, optional intake_conditions: food with | without | either, meal_timing { relation before | after, minutes }, fasting fasted | not_fasted | either, take_with and avoid_with chips from dairy, fat, calcium, iron, coffee plus take_with_other / avoid_with_other free text). Alternatively send the optional per-item form instead of shaping the prescription yourself: form "powder" with strength_amount/strength_unit as the mass (e.g. 10, "g") saves quantity 1; form "liquid" with amount as the volume in mL (e.g. 5) saves no strength; a count form (capsule, tablet, softgel, …) keeps amount as the count and strength_amount/strength_unit as what one contains. The time of day decides the group it is shown in. Pass subject "dog" to replace your own dog's supplement stack instead (needs My dog on; kept apart from yours and from any coach); omitted means your own. If your coach assigned your supplements, only timing and reminders change; the coach's items and doses are kept. Requires the upload terms, accepted once in the Fysigo app.

**Reads or writes:** write (replaces existing content) · safe to repeat · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `protocols:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | array of object | yes |  |
| `subject` | `me` \| `dog` | no |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- The stack you send replaces the stored one as a whole. An item you leave out is removed.
- A change made in the app after your last get_my_protocols is overwritten. Read again just before saving.
- When your coach assigned the stack, your item and dose changes are ignored on this save and only timing, reminders and notes are kept. After that save Fysigo records you as the stack's author, so a later save can change items too. Read it back with get_my_protocols to see what was kept.
- Supplement groups and links to the supplement catalog are not kept: each item is placed by its time of day.
- An item sent without intake_conditions is saved with none. A coach-assigned stack keeps the coach's intake_conditions, and a dog stack does not keep intake_conditions.

## `get_my_doses_today`

Today's peptide and supplement doses in your own time zone (or, with date, one past day inside the 7-day decision window: today minus 6 through tomorrow), each with its time, amount and whether it is already logged (done, skipped, missed or pending). A compound with several dose lines has one entry per line, each with that line's own amount. Each entry carries the kind, assignmentId and occurrenceKey that log_my_dose needs. Pass subject "dog" for your own dog's log; omitted means your own and never includes dog rows.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `protocols:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `subject` | `me` \| `dog` | no |  |
| `date` | string | no | `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Today is your profile's time zone, not the client's local clock.
- date reaches back 6 days (the decision window); an older day is refused with date_outside_window and nothing is listed.
- As-needed doses have no fixed slot and are not listed.

## `log_my_dose`

Mark one dose as done or skipped (today's, or a past one from the last 7 days), with an optional taken_at (when it was actually taken; default now), using kind, assignmentId and occurrenceKey exactly as get_my_doses_today returned them (pass its date for a past day). Logging the same dose again with the same status and no taken_at changes nothing; with a taken_at it edits the recorded take time; a new status replaces the old one and records the new time. Using the assignmentId from get_my_doses_today with subject "dog" it also logs that dose on your dog's log; ownership is enforced by the route.

**Reads or writes:** write · safe to repeat · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `protocols:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `peptide` \| `supplement` | yes |  |
| `assignmentId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `occurrenceKey` | string | yes | `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` |
| `status` | `done` \| `skipped` | yes |  |
| `taken_at` | string | no | `^(?:(?:\d\d[2468][048]\|\d\d[13579][26]\|\d\d0[48]\|[02468][048]00\|[13579][26]00)-02-29\|\d{4}-(?:(?:0[13578]\|1[02])-(?:0[1-9]\|[12]\d\|3[01])\|(?:0[469]\|11)-(?:0[1-9]\|[12]\d\|30)\|(?:02)-(?:0[1-9]\|1\d\|2[0-8])))T(?:(?:[01]\d\|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d:[0-5]\d(?:\.\d+)?(?:Z\|([+-](?:[01]\d\|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d)))$` |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- taken_at outside the dose's decision window (older than its day or in the future) is refused with invalid_occurred_at; nothing is logged.
- Read get_my_doses_today (with date for a past day) right before logging: the occurrenceKey is derived from the dose's current state.
- Logging an already-logged dose again with a taken_at EDITS its recorded take time (same status, one row, vial draw-down untouched). Without taken_at a repeat is a no-op.
- A peptide dose logged as done draws down the active product in the app's inventory, as it does when logged on the phone.

## `backfill_my_dose`

Log ONE dose that already happened, on any past date and time (no 7-day limit), with the amount you actually took. No schedule or active assignment is needed. Peptide: send compoundName (or compoundId from search_peptide_compounds), amount and unit (mcg, mg or labelled dose), optionally vialInUseId and note. Supplement: send the itemId of the item in your stack (read get_my_protocols); its as-needed doses are appended at takenAt, scheduled items get that day confirmed at takenAt. takenAt may not be in the future. Sending the same dose again never double-logs: it comes back as duplicate. For many doses use import_my_dose_history.

**Reads or writes:** write · safe to repeat · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `protocols:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `peptide` \| `supplement` | yes |  |
| `compoundName` | string | no |  |
| `compoundId` | string (uuid) | no |  |
| `itemId` | string | no |  |
| `takenAt` | string | yes | `^(?:(?:\d\d[2468][048]\|\d\d[13579][26]\|\d\d0[48]\|[02468][048]00\|[13579][26]00)-02-29\|\d{4}-(?:(?:0[13578]\|1[02])-(?:0[1-9]\|[12]\d\|3[01])\|(?:0[469]\|11)-(?:0[1-9]\|[12]\d\|30)\|(?:02)-(?:0[1-9]\|1\d\|2[0-8])))T(?:(?:[01]\d\|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d:[0-5]\d(?:\.\d+)?(?:Z\|([+-](?:[01]\d\|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d)))$` |
| `amount` | number | no |  |
| `unit` | `mcg` \| `ug` \| `µg` \| `μg` \| `mg` \| `labelled dose` | no |  |
| `vialInUseId` | string (uuid) | no |  |
| `note` | string | no |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- A peptide dose is matched on compound + takenAt + amount; a supplement dose on item + takenAt (as-needed) or item + day (scheduled).
- Supplement amounts come from the stack item; send amount only if it equals the item's amount. A supplement that is not in your stack is refused with supplement_item_not_found.
- A manual peptide backfill does not change vial inventory unless a vialInUseId is sent.

## `import_my_dose_history`

Bulk-load past doses: up to 300 rows per call, each shaped like backfill_my_dose (kind, compoundName or compoundId or itemId, takenAt, amount, unit). Any past date, no assignment needed, future times refused. Every row is independent and gets its own result - created, duplicate (already logged, skipped) or error with a reason - so a bad row never blocks the rest. Safe to rerun with the same rows: nothing is logged twice. Load vial mixes first (mix_my_vial, oldest first) if the doses should draw down a vial via vialInUseId.

**Reads or writes:** write · safe to repeat · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `protocols:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rows` | array of object | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Rows are deduplicated in code on compound + takenAt + amount (peptides) and item + takenAt or day (supplements); a database-level unique index is a follow-up.
- Results carry the row's index in the order you sent; error rows write nothing.
- Supplement rows need the item in your stack; peptide rows work with a name alone.

## `scan_my_supplement_label`

Read a supplement bottle from 1-3 photos (front label, Supplement Facts panel), exactly like the app's Add from photo: returns the product name, brand, form, serving size, every ingredient with its amount and unit per serving, and the package count when printed. Send each photo as base64 (imageBase64, at most 1 MB) with its mimeType. The photos are kept privately for you (only you can see them) when you have accepted the upload terms, and uploadId names that private scan; photosKept says whether they were kept. With addToCatalog true it also confirms the parsed label in Fysigo's shared catalog, which holds label data only and never your photos, and returns the catalogId. The same product scanned by anyone resolves to one canonical entry. Pass stackItemId to link the scan to that stack item. It never adds anything to your stack (use save_my_supplement_stack for that).

**Reads or writes:** write · safe to repeat · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `protocols:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `anthropicPhotoConsent` | boolean | no |  |
| `photos` | array of object | yes |  |
| `addToCatalog` | boolean | no |  |
| `stackItemId` | string | no |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Photos are kept only in your private storage, never in the shared catalog and never shown to anyone else; without the upload terms they are analysed and not kept. A label the reader cannot read with confidence is refused as unreadable_label; unknown values come back null, never guessed.
- Amounts are per the printed serving, not a personal dose. A new catalog entry stays pending and visible only to you until Fysigo reviews it; once reviewed, everyone's matching scans point to the same entry.

## `preview_my_lab_import`

Preview your own structured lab values or an existing uploaded PDF. Uses the app's marker catalog, matching and unit conversions; reports matched, ambiguous, unknown, duplicate and conflicting rows. Writes no lab results. Review every row with the human, then pass only the short-lived previewToken to confirm_my_lab_import. Supply values OR uploadId, never both.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `bloodwork:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `values` | array of object | no |  |
| `uploadId` | string (uuid) | no |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- No lab results are written by preview. The standard AI-action and PHI access audit records contain no values.
- Unknown, ambiguous, unsupported-unit and conflicting rows block the whole confirmation. Fix the source and preview again; no marker is guessed.
- Duplicate detection uses the same bloodwork history the app reads (up to 5000 stored markers); it cannot establish completeness beyond that window.
- Censored, qualitative and multiple-draw PDFs require the app's review flow. Codes absent from the marker catalog remain unknown.
- The preview expires in 15 minutes and is bound to this account and connection. It does not establish clinical correctness.

## `confirm_my_lab_import`

Confirm a lab import the human has reviewed using preview_my_lab_import. Accepts ONLY the exact previewToken, never new values or a client id. Writes only your own results through the web app's save service. Repeat-safe on the token: deterministic result/marker ids prevent duplicate rows. Requires bloodwork:write; never confirm without the human's approval of that preview.

**Reads or writes:** write · safe to repeat · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `bloodwork:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `previewToken` | string | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Only unambiguous, supported, nonduplicate rows from the reviewed preview are saved. Expired previews must be recreated and reviewed.
- A multi-date import may partially complete if storage becomes unavailable. Retry the same token before expiry; saved rows are repeat-safe.
- Saved counts describe the preview's accepted rows, including a replay; they do not claim clinical correctness or that every possible marker was supplied.

**What a result cannot tell you**

## `get_my_day`

Your whole Now timeline for today in one call — the same feed the iPhone's Now screen shows: meals, workouts, doses, sleep and the day's other items, each with its label, time and status, plus which items are still upcoming and which are past. Read this first when the person asks what their day looks like, what is next, or whether something was done today. It needs the protocols, training, sleep and nutrition scopes because the feed can carry doses, workouts, nights and meals.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `protocols:read` + `training:read` + `sleep:read` + `nutrition:read`

No arguments.

**What a result cannot tell you**

- setupRequired true means the app still needs its one-time setup before the timeline has anything on it.
- Items are the app's projections of the day; an item the member never logged (for example a meal they did not record) simply does not appear.

Notes are kept unless you send them (null clears). Only the fields that activity type has can be set (see fields from get_my_activity); a type with no fields can only change its notes. Watch readings (heart rate, distance, energy) are kept and cannot be edited. Returns the activity as stored.

No arguments.

Move one of your queued workouts to another day. In a rolling queue this pins the card to a date (null puts it back in queue order); in a calendar program it changes the scheduled date. scheduledWorkoutId comes from get_my_workout_queue. Returns the card as it is now.

| `scheduledWorkoutId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `date` | any | yes |  |

## `get_my_dose_history`

Your peptide dose history over a date range (default: the last 30 days, at most 90): per protocol the prescribed dose count and how many were confirmed, missed or skipped, plus the individual dose slots with their status and takenAt (when the dose was actually logged as taken or skipped, ISO-8601; null for a missed slot). Pass subject "dog" for your own dog's assignments (needs My dog on); omitted means your own and never includes dog rows. This is the same projection the app's peptide trends page shows.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `protocols:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | string | no | `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` |
| `to` | string | no | `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` |
| `subject` | `me` \| `dog` | no |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Counts only your active protocol assignments: a paused or ended protocol is not included, so its earlier doses are missing from the counts.
- prescribed is projected from the protocol's schedule rules; a dose line the protocol does not structure cannot be counted as prescribed.
- The logs list is capped at 500 slots; a wider window may cut off older slots.

## `get_my_doses_range`

Every peptide and supplement dose of your own between two dates, the same list the app's Peptide timeline and Supplement timeline show: scheduled doses still to come, doses taken or skipped, missed scheduled doses, and doses loaded with backfill_my_dose or import_my_dose_history that have no protocol assignment. Each row has kind, item, dose (in the dose's own units, e.g. 250 mcg, 3 capsules, 3 g), at (ISO-8601 take time when logged, else the scheduled time), date and time in your time zone, status (taken, skipped, missed, due, scheduled), backfilled (logged on a later day than it was taken), oneOff (logged outside any schedule) and asNeeded. from/to are local dates (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive), at most 62 days per call; earlier and later name the neighbouring windows for the next call. Rows come oldest first, 500 per page by default (limit up to 1000); pass nextOffset as offset for the rest. kind is peptide, supplement or all (default all). Read only.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `protocols:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | string | yes | `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` |
| `to` | string | yes | `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` |
| `kind` | `peptide` \| `supplement` \| `all` | no |  |
| `offset` | integer | no |  |
| `limit` | integer | no |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Only your own doses: never a dog's and never another member's.
- dose is display text; the same dose may read differently once a protocol's units change.
- missed, due and scheduled rows are projected from your current and paused protocols; an ended protocol only shows the doses that were logged.
- peptides is not_available when peptide tracking is off for your account; kind all then returns supplements only.
- Supplement reads are recorded in the health data audit log.

## `get_my_protocol_history`

Every saved version of your own peptide protocols, oldest first: protocol id, version number, effective_from (when that version took effect, ISO-8601), the full snapshot (items with dose amount and unit, route, local time, weekdays 1-7 with 1 = Monday, schedule rules, cycle) and a diff against the previous version (item_added, item_removed, dose_changed, days_changed, time_changed, schedule_rules_changed, cycle_changed, status_changed, renamed). Use it with get_my_dose_history (which carries takenAt per dose) and get_my_sleep to line protocol changes up against sleep, HRV, resting heart rate and training. from/to are local dates (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive) on effective_from; omit both for all history. Pass protocol_id for one protocol. Pass subject "dog" for your own dog's protocols; omitted means your own and never includes dog rows.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `protocols:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | string | no | `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` |
| `to` | string | no | `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` |
| `protocol_id` | string (uuid) | no |  |
| `subject` | `me` \| `dog` | no |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- History starts with the first save after version tracking shipped (2026-11); earlier changes to a protocol were not kept.
- A version is recorded after the save commits; if recording failed, that save is missing and the next version's diff spans both changes.
- To see what was active on a day, take the latest version whose effective_from is before it; a version before your from date is not returned.
- At most 500 versions per call; truncated is true when more exist.

## `get_my_supplement_stack_history`

Every saved version of your own supplement stack, oldest first: version number, effective_from (ISO-8601), the full snapshot (items with amount and unit, strength, local time, weekdays 1-7 with 1 = Monday) and a diff against the previous version (item_added, item_removed, dose_changed, days_changed, time_changed, schedule_rules_changed, status_changed, renamed). Use it with get_my_sleep and your training reads to line stack changes up against sleep, HRV, resting heart rate and training. from/to are local dates (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive) on effective_from; omit both for all history.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `protocols:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | string | no | `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` |
| `to` | string | no | `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- History starts with the first save after version tracking shipped (2026-11); earlier stack changes were not kept.
- A version is recorded after the save commits; if recording failed, that save is missing and the next version's diff spans both changes.
- Saves made by a coach on your behalf are recorded only when they go through the same save as the app; a coach-side edit may be missing.
- At most 500 versions per call; truncated is true when more exist.

## `get_my_uvb_window`

How long you need in the sun today to make your vitamin D: the window when the sun is high enough (from your saved location), today's clear-sky UV index, and the minutes centred on solar noon to make a target amount of vitamin D for your skin and how much of it is in the sun. When skin is not passed, your saved skin tone is used (set it with set_my_skin_tone or estimate_my_skin_tone_from_photo; skinSource in the result says which).

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `settings:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | string | no | `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` |
| `skin` | `pale` \| `light_tan` \| `tanned` \| `deep_tan` \| `brown` \| `dark` | no |  |
| `exposure` | `face_hands` \| `tshirt_shorts` \| `shirtless_shorts` \| `swimsuit` \| `naked` | no |  |
| `targetIu` | integer | no |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Clear-sky estimate from sun position and seasonal ozone: clouds, glass and shade lower the real UVB. IU are model estimates, roughly ±2×.
- A deeper tan makes less vitamin D per minute: the saved tone ages as you tan or fade. skinSource "default" means no tone is saved and tanned was assumed.

## `set_my_skin_tone`

Save your skin tone today for the vitamin D calculator (pale, light_tan, tanned, deep_tan, brown or dark). A deeper tan makes less vitamin D per minute, so get_my_uvb_window gives more minutes.

**Reads or writes:** write · safe to repeat · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `settings:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `skinTone` | `pale` \| `light_tan` \| `tanned` \| `deep_tan` \| `brown` \| `dark` | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Saving the same tone again changes nothing. A tone you set by hand stays until you save a new one or estimate one from a photo.

## `estimate_my_skin_tone_from_photo`

Estimate your skin tone today from one photo and save it for the vitamin D calculator, exactly like the photo button in the app's UVB window tool. Send the photo as base64 (imageBase64) with its mimeType (image/jpeg, image/png or image/webp, at most 10 MB). The photo is analysed and not stored. Requires upload terms and explicit permission to send this photo to Anthropic for skin-tone analysis.

**Reads or writes:** write · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `settings:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `imageBase64` | string | yes |  |
| `mimeType` | `image/jpeg` \| `image/png` \| `image/webp` | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- The photo is analysed and not stored. Lighting and filters change how skin looks; set it by hand with set_my_skin_tone if the result is off.

## `list_my_listings`

List the marketplace product listings you authored: each with its type, title, price, status, the draft revision and the current published version. Only your own listings; buyers find published products elsewhere.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Coach · **Scope:** `marketplace:read`

No arguments.

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Lists only listings you authored. Published listings by other creators are not included.
- Review fields (review decision, note, draft revision) appear because you are the author; buyers never see them.

## `create_listing`

Create a marketplace product listing as a draft: a recipe, a peptide protocol or a bundle. Requires the coach or admin role and the upload terms accepted once in the Fysigo app. Nothing is published or on sale: the listing stays a draft until submit_listing, admin review and publish_listing. Prices are whole dollars (priceCents must be a multiple of 100; 1999 is refused). Send pricingModel "free" with no priceCents for a free product. Content is required and validated against the type's schema now; change it later with update_listing or the typed editors.

**Reads or writes:** write · **Plan:** Coach · **Scope:** `marketplace:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `businessId` | string (uuid) | no |  |
| `type` | `recipe` \| `peptide_protocol` \| `bundle` | yes |  |
| `title` | string | yes |  |
| `summary` | string | no |  |
| `priceCents` | integer | no |  |
| `currency` | string | no |  |
| `pricingModel` | `free` \| `one_time` \| `subscription` | no |  |
| `content` | any | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- With businessId, current business content authority and business:products-write are required; the business owner is the merchant and your author credit is retained.
- The listing is created as a private draft: it is not visible to buyers and cannot be bought until it has been submitted, approved in review and published.

## `update_listing`

Edit your own listing while it is a draft or has changes requested: title, summary, price (whole dollars only), currency, pricing model, and draft content. Editing bumps the draft revision and clears any approval bound to the earlier revision, so an approved listing returns to needing review. Authors only; published content already sold is never changed — buyers keep their pinned version.

**Reads or writes:** write (replaces existing content) · **Plan:** Coach · **Scope:** `marketplace:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `productId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `patch` | object | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- A shared storefront product also requires business:products-write and current content permission; merchant identity cannot be changed through this tool.
- The patch replaces the fields you send. A changed draft content invalidates an earlier approval: after editing, submit_listing and a fresh review are required before publish_listing works.
- This result does not confirm the listing is still in a draft state; a concurrent submit or review changes what is editable. Read list_my_listings before a retry.

## `submit_listing`

Submit your draft (or a changes-requested listing you edited) for admin review. The content is validated against the product type's schema and bundle references are resolved and frozen; the review decision lands in list_my_listings. Submitting does not publish and does not put the listing on sale. A bundle that references programs additionally requires the programs:read scope: freezing a program's content into the bundle reads that private program data, so a marketplace-only token is refused before anything is read or written. References to marketplace products, documents, videos and inline stacks need nothing beyond marketplace:write.

**Reads or writes:** write · **Plan:** Coach · **Scope:** `marketplace:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `productId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- A shared storefront product also requires business:products-write and current content permission; merchant identity cannot be changed through this tool.
- The review decision is made in Fysigo's admin review, not by this tool. Watch list_my_listings for reviewDecision: approved, declined or changes_requested.
- A bundle's referenced programs and products are frozen at submit: later edits to the sources do not change this submission.

## `publish_listing`

Publish a reviewed listing: creates the immutable version buyers purchase and puts the listing on sale. Requires the review decision approved against the current draft revision, the upload terms, and a connected, payable Stripe account. A draft edited after approval must be submitted and approved again first.

**Reads or writes:** write · **Plan:** Coach · **Scope:** `marketplace:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `productId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- New paid publication requires a recorded business merchant and an active provider plan; an unbound paid draft cannot be published. Existing purchases keep their accepted terms.
- A shared storefront product also requires business:products-write and current content permission; merchant identity cannot be changed through this tool.
- Publishing a changed draft creates a new version; buyers of the earlier version stay pinned to the one they bought.
- This result does not say whether a payout has settled; Stripe settlement state is not part of it.

## `get_sales`

Your product sales as the seller sees them: each purchase of your listings with the product title, version, amount, currency, status and when it was purchased. Buyers appear as ids only — no buyer health data. Coach package.

## `read_product`

Read one marketplace product: the sanitized listing (type, title, summary, price, status) and, when you are entitled, the payload of the version pinned to you. Entitlement is a live paid purchase of the product (the author reads the current version instead). A bundle lists its items with a per-item entitlement flag: separately purchased items read fully, and items covered only by this bundle read within it. Peptide dose and cycle fields stay redacted until you acknowledge the terms for that version with acknowledge_protocol; protocol items inside a bundle are gated the same way. A refund or dispute ends the read access.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `marketplace:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `productId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Without a live paid purchase (or authorship) the payload is not included: content is null and contentError says why. The listing itself is public while published.
- Protocol doses and cycle fields are redacted until acknowledge_protocol for the pinned version; the listing and item structure read either way.
- Bundle video items are external public links, not protected media.
- Stripe settlement state (refund in progress, dispute) is not part of this read; a completed refund or an open dispute is.

Acknowledge the peptide protocol terms for one product version, by its termsVersion. Required before the dose and cycle fields of that protocol's payload are shown to you (standalone protocol or protocol items inside a bundle), and before adopt_protocol. Requires a live paid purchase of the product, or authorship. Acknowledging the same version and terms again changes nothing.

- Acknowledging for one version does not cover other versions of the same product.

## `adopt_protocol`

Copy a purchased protocol product version into your own peptide protocols, as the app's personal save does: you get a caller-owned draft you can edit, dose-track and keep after a refund. Requires a live paid purchase of that exact version and acknowledge_protocol for it first, and BOTH the marketplace:write and protocols:write scopes — adopting writes your personal protocols, so a marketplace-only token is never enough. The adopted draft is created through the same personal save path as the app, with your own JWT; the marketplace records only the provenance. Repeating the call returns the existing adoption and saves nothing.

**Reads or writes:** write · safe to repeat · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `marketplace:write` + `protocols:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `versionId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Adopting copies the published version's items; edits you make to your copy never change the listing, and later listing versions never change your copy.
- Adoption refuses honestly instead of inventing: an item without an authored dose, unit, route, time or explicit weekly schedule, or carrying cycle weeks, rejects the adoption naming the compounds — the person configures those in the app. The adopted draft is saved paused with reminders off; activating it is their explicit decision.
- The saved draft starts without vial products: mix_my_vial records the first vial, as with any self-authored protocol.
- If the final provenance write fails after the personal save succeeded, your copy exists in get_my_protocols but the adoption is not recorded; the message says so.

## `list_my_business_operations`

List the business operations you effectively hold on one of your provider businesses: the owner holds every operation (manage_staff, manage_schedule_self, manage_schedule_team, manage_storefront, manage_content, manage_billing, manage_chat) by ownership; accepted active staff hold only what was granted to them. manage_chat is the customer-conversation access operation — it names who may access the business's conversation history; no tool here reads message content. Coach tier. Needs the business:read scope.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Coach · **Scope:** `business:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `businessId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- An operation is effective only while your membership is accepted and active and your account and tenant stay live: a removal, ban or tenant move takes it away at the next call.
- Staff hold only granted operations. The owner holds every operation by ownership and it never appears as a grant row.
- A granted operation authorizes the matching business tool for it (manage_billing exists for the business billing tools); the tools themselves read no clinical records and move no money. Health-data sharing and platform admin stay separate surfaces. manage_chat grants staff access to the business's customer-conversation history. This MCP tool only changes that access; it does not let the connected AI read messages.

## `list_business_operation_grants`

List the operation-grant history (live and revoked) for one member of a provider business you own or manage. Rows are limited to what you may read: the business owner, the member themself while pending or active, or a live manage_staff holder; anyone else gets nothing. Revoked rows (revokedAt set) are history, not effective grants. Coach tier. Needs the business:read scope.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Coach · **Scope:** `business:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `businessId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `memberProfileId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- An empty grants list can mean the member has no grants OR that this account may not read them — Fysigo answers the same way for both.
- grants includes revoked rows for audit: revokedAt not null marks history, never an effective grant.
- A grant authorizes the named business tool only. The tools in this unit read no clinical records and move no money; health-data sharing and platform admin stay separate.

## `set_business_operation`

Grant (enabled=true) or revoke (enabled=false) one business operation — manage_staff, manage_schedule_self, manage_schedule_team, manage_storefront, manage_content, manage_billing or manage_chat — for one named member of a provider business. Owner only: the database re-checks ownership under a lock, the member's membership state, and the member's live identity and current tenant on every call, so manage_staff can never grant and a removed or tenant-moved member can never be granted. A grant stored for a pending invitee is inert until they accept. Revocation keeps durable history. manage_chat — staff access to all past and future customer conversations of the business — additionally requires the business:chat-manage scope for BOTH grant and revoke, and it grants conversation access only: it never lets this AI read messages or any clinical record. Coach tier. Needs the business:write scope (and business:chat-manage for manage_chat).

**Reads or writes:** write (replaces existing content) · safe to repeat · **Plan:** Coach · **Scope:** `business:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `businessId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `memberProfileId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `operation` | `manage_staff` \| `manage_schedule_self` \| `manage_schedule_team` \| `manage_storefront` \| `manage_content` \| `manage_billing` \| `manage_chat` | yes |  |
| `enabled` | boolean | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- The owner holds every operation by ownership and can never be a grant target: targeting the owner fails.
- manage_staff does not authorize this tool — only the business owner can grant or revoke, and a grant authorizes the named business operation only: the tools here read no clinical records, move no money, and never touch health-data sharing or platform admin.
- manage_chat is the only operation with a second scope: business:write AND business:chat-manage are required for both grant and revoke, and a token carrying only one of them is refused before the database is asked. The grant covers all past and future customer conversations of the business, but this tool reads no messages and grants no clinical permission — no message-reading tool exists in this server.
- A grant stored for a pending invitee confers nothing until they accept; a removed member must be re-invited before they can be granted again.
- Revocation preserves durable history and never revives: after remove → re-invite → re-accept, a previously revoked grant stays revoked until a new grant is stored.
- The result confirms the database's decision (the enabled value it returns); it is NOT a read-back of the grant rows. Call list_business_operation_grants to see them.

Registration makes someone bookable — it grants no other operation permission, and it creates no booking, checkout, customer record or payment. Coach tier. Needs the business:write scope.

| `endsAt` | string | yes | `^(?:(?:\d\d[2468][048]\|\d\d[13579][26]\|\d\d0[48]\|[02468][048]00\|[13579][26]00)-02-29\|\d{4}-(?:(?:0[13578]\|1[02])-(?:0[1-9]\|[12]\d\|3[01])\|(?:0[469]\|11)-(?:0[1-9]\|[12]\d\|30)\|(?:02)-(?:0[1-9]\|1\d\|2[0-8])))T(?:(?:[01]\d\|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d:[0-5]\d(?:\.\d+)?(?:Z\|([+-](?:[01]\d\|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d)))$` |
| `timeZone` | string | yes |  |
| `windowId` | string (uuid) | no |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- The result confirms the new window id the database stored; it is NOT a read-back. Call business_read_calendar to see live windows.
- A window is availability, never a reservation: nothing is held against a customer's booking, and busy intervals from business_read_calendar show conflicts only.
- An edit retires the old window and creates a replacement; the retired row is history and is never returned by the read tools.

## `business_retire_availability_window`

Terminally retire one availability window of a provider business. Same authority as the write (owner, manage_schedule_team, or the practitioner with manage_schedule_self); the target practitioner is inferred from the window after the business is authorized. Retiring an already-retired window is allowed for an authorized caller and changes nothing. This never touches any booking or the personal calendar — it removes availability only. Coach tier. Needs the business:write scope.

**Reads or writes:** write (replaces existing content) · safe to repeat · **Plan:** Coach · **Scope:** `business:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `businessId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `windowId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- The result confirms the database's decision (true when a live window was retired); it is NOT a read-back of the window rows.
- Retirement is terminal: the window never reappears in business_read_calendar, and no existing or future booking is created, changed, or cancelled by it.

## `business_read_practitioner_setup`

Read one provider business's bookable setup: registered practitioners (with display name and public-bookable flag), bound appointment services, and service-to-practitioner assignments. The exact owner additionally receives availableSources: their same-tenant active non-client-private massage services and one-to-one offerings, including unbound sources, with opaque id/name/sourceKind for binding. Owner, manage_staff, or a schedule reader; a manage_schedule_self holder sees only their own registration and assignments. Bounded projections — no member email, no customer identity, no clinical, note, or financial fields, and no retired history. Coach tier. Needs the business:read scope.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Coach · **Scope:** `business:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `businessId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- What you see depends on your operations: the owner, manage_staff and schedule readers see the business setup; a manage_schedule_self holder sees only their own practitioner row and assignments. Fysigo answers the same bounded shape for both.
- Only live registrations, live bindings and live assignments are returned: a retired row is history and never appears here, and an assignment whose binding or source went stale disappears from the projection.
- availableSources is owner-only and includes eligible unbound sources before any practitioner registration exists. Staff receive an empty array, not the owner's or their own unbound catalog. Match sourceKind and id when binding; never guess an opaque source ID. A source-read failure is an error, not proof that the catalog is empty.
- displayName is the practitioner's own full name; there is no member email, no customer data, and no clinical or financial fields in this surface.

## `business_read_calendar`

Read one provider business's availability for a date range (positive, at most 93 days): the dated availability windows of its registered practitioners (or one practitioner via profileId) plus anonymous busy intervals for the same targets. Owner or team schedule readers; a manage_schedule_self holder reads only their own windows and busy, and manage_staff alone cannot read the calendar. Busy is a conflict signal, not a reservation: each busy row carries ONLY practitionerId, startsAt, endsAt — never the underlying booking, its id, customer, business, reason, money, or health data. Windows and busy never create, hold, or change a booking. Coach tier. Needs the business:read scope.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Coach · **Scope:** `business:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `businessId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `rangeStart` | string | yes | `^(?:(?:\d\d[2468][048]\|\d\d[13579][26]\|\d\d0[48]\|[02468][048]00\|[13579][26]00)-02-29\|\d{4}-(?:(?:0[13578]\|1[02])-(?:0[1-9]\|[12]\d\|3[01])\|(?:0[469]\|11)-(?:0[1-9]\|[12]\d\|30)\|(?:02)-(?:0[1-9]\|1\d\|2[0-8])))T(?:(?:[01]\d\|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d:[0-5]\d(?:\.\d+)?(?:Z\|([+-](?:[01]\d\|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d)))$` |
| `rangeEnd` | string | yes | `^(?:(?:\d\d[2468][048]\|\d\d[13579][26]\|\d\d0[48]\|[02468][048]00\|[13579][26]00)-02-29\|\d{4}-(?:(?:0[13578]\|1[02])-(?:0[1-9]\|[12]\d\|3[01])\|(?:0[469]\|11)-(?:0[1-9]\|[12]\d\|30)\|(?:02)-(?:0[1-9]\|1\d\|2[0-8])))T(?:(?:[01]\d\|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d:[0-5]\d(?:\.\d+)?(?:Z\|([+-](?:[01]\d\|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d)))$` |
| `profileId` | string (uuid) | no |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Busy reflects conflicts across the practitioner's whole schedule (existing bookings and blocks) but is not a reservation guarantee; it says when they are occupied, never why or for whom.
- Busy rows expose exactly practitionerId/startsAt/endsAt. The source booking, its business, the customer, any note, and any money or health fields are deliberately not part of this surface.
- The range is capped at 93 days and the result fails rather than silently truncating when the business exceeds the row caps; narrow the range or target and read again.

## `read_shared_records`

Read one page of health records a client shared with you under an explicit provider-scoped grant for one domain. The actor is always your signed-in account (the named provider or staff with inherited access) — clientId and providerId only name the grant, not who is calling. Same serialized shape as the desktop owner preview. Coach tier. Needs the sharing:read scope. Owner consent is granted only in the Fysigo app; calling this tool does not request or approve sharing.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Coach · **Scope:** `sharing:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clientId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `providerId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `domain` | `peptide_protocol` \| `peptide_logs` \| `training_program` \| `training_logs` \| `nutrition_plan` \| `nutrition_logs` \| `bloodwork` \| `sleep` \| `progress_photos` \| `general_checkins` | yes |  |
| `cursor` | string | no |  |
| `locale` | `en` \| `es` | no |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- The actor is always the MCP token holder verified as provider or inherited active staff for this grant — never inferred from clientId or providerId.
- loadedCount is the number of records on this page only; hasMore means another page may exist under the same grant.
- When gaps is present, those source streams are unavailable on this deployment; hasMore=false with gaps means complete for working streams only, not that every source in the domain is covered.
- Owner consent to share requires the Fysigo app; an access request or this read tool does not grant sharing.
- Generic coach client reach and staff expansion never apply — only explicit provider-scoped v2 grants authorize rows.
- Read-only: no create, edit, revoke or policy change through MCP.

## `schedule_community_live`

Schedule a live video session in a community space you manage: title, start and end (ISO instants), IANA time zone, and an optional exact membership-tier pin (tierId and tierVersionId together). Returns the session id and an authenticated join link for the app — never a video room URL or token. Requires the communities:live-write scope.

**Reads or writes:** write · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `communities:live-write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `spaceId` | string | yes |  |
| `title` | string | yes |  |
| `description` | string | no |  |
| `startsAt` | string | yes |  |
| `endsAt` | string | yes |  |
| `timeZone` | string | yes |  |
| `tierId` | string or null | no |  |
| `tierVersionId` | string or null | no |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- The join link is an authenticated Fysigo app route: opening it requires a signed-in session with community access. This tool never returns a Daily room URL or a meeting token.
- Fysigo checks current community access for reads and current management permission for writes on every call; a live MCP scope is never itself a business permission.
- Scheduling records the session in the named space only; it does not check that the time slot is free and it does not issue any video room or token.

- Sessions in a space this account may not read are omitted or refused by the live SQL authority; an empty list does not distinguish no sessions from no access.

## `get_product_publication_state`

Read marketplace and per-business storefront listing flags for one product you authored. Only the product author can call this; storefront bindings list each business id and whether the product is storefront-listed there. Coach tier. Needs the marketplace:read scope.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Coach · **Scope:** `marketplace:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `productId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Discovery flags only: this does not submit or approve a listing, change entitlements, or read product payload content.
- Storefront-listed on a binding does not mean the business storefront is effectively public — use read_business_storefront_publication for the live visibility predicate.
- Turning marketplace listing off blocks new marketplace discovery and checkout; existing purchases and membership inclusions pinned to a version stay entitled.
- Monthly membership checkout exists as quote_provider_membership_checkout + start_provider_membership_checkout, but it is disabled by default on this deployment (FYSIGO_PROVIDER_MEMBERSHIP_CHECKOUT_ENABLED unset) and refuses before any payment effect until an operator enables it.

## `list_business_bound_products_for_publishing`

List products bound to one provider business with marketplace and storefront discovery flags for publishing review. Business owner or manage_storefront on that business. Coach tier. Needs the business:read scope.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Coach · **Scope:** `business:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `businessId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `limit` | integer | no |  |
| `offset` | integer | no |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Lists bindings only — not every product you authored unless it is bound to this business.
- Discovery flags do not grant buyers access; entitlements follow purchases and membership pins.
- hasMore means another page may exist under the same filters.
- Monthly membership checkout exists as quote_provider_membership_checkout + start_provider_membership_checkout, but it is disabled by default on this deployment (FYSIGO_PROVIDER_MEMBERSHIP_CHECKOUT_ENABLED unset) and refuses before any payment effect until an operator enables it.

## `list_business_tiers_for_publishing`

List membership tiers for one provider business with publishing metadata (price, cadence, publishedAt). Business owner or manage_storefront. Coach tier. Needs the business:read scope.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Coach · **Scope:** `business:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `businessId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `limit` | integer | no |  |
| `offset` | integer | no |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- This read does not create subscriptions, run Stripe checkout, or grant entitlements through MCP.
- Monthly tiers may already show publishedAt once published and activated in the backend; do not assume every row is still a draft.
- Only free tiers can be published or joined through the existing membership MCP tools today.
- hasMore means another page may exist under the same filters.

## `list_tier_product_inclusions`

List products included in one membership tier with the pinned product version id for each inclusion. Business owner or manage_storefront for the tier's business. Coach tier. Needs the business:read scope.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Coach · **Scope:** `business:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tierId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `limit` | integer | no |  |
| `offset` | integer | no |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Inclusions pin a specific product version; changing the product's current version does not move existing pins until you update the tier.
- Removing an inclusion or cancelling membership stops included access without revoking separate purchases.
- hasMore means another page may exist under the same filters.

## `read_business_storefront_publication`

Report whether a provider business storefront is effectively public right now, using the same SQL predicate as anonymous discovery (published storefront plus active business and owner live-identity and capability gates). Coach tier. Needs the business:read scope.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Coach · **Scope:** `business:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `businessId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- storefrontPublic is the live public visibility check, not a private read of published_at alone; failed gates read false even when a storefront row exists.
- false does not distinguish an unknown business id from an unpublished storefront or a failed gate — do not treat false as proof the business exists.
- Not per-product storefront listing flags; an unpublished storefront hides public discovery and new bookings without cancelling existing bookings.
- This read does not change listing flags or approve marketplace products.

## `set_product_marketplace_listing`

Turn global Fysigo Marketplace discovery on or off for one product you authored. Only the product author; SQL stores the listing flag only — published and approved status is enforced when buyers discover the product, not when you set the flag. Coach tier. Needs the marketplace:write scope.

**Reads or writes:** write · safe to repeat · **Plan:** Coach · **Scope:** `marketplace:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `productId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `marketplaceListed` | boolean | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Discovery only — not admin approval, not publishing a new product version, and not a purchase or entitlement grant.
- marketplaceListed true does not make an unpublished or unapproved product discoverable; discovery requires published, approved, and listed.
- Listing off blocks new marketplace checkout; existing purchases and membership version pins stay entitled.
- Monthly membership checkout exists as quote_provider_membership_checkout + start_provider_membership_checkout, but it is disabled by default on this deployment (FYSIGO_PROVIDER_MEMBERSHIP_CHECKOUT_ENABLED unset) and refuses before any payment effect until an operator enables it.

## `set_product_storefront_listing`

Turn storefront discovery on or off for one product bound to a provider business. Product author, business owner, or manage_storefront on that business; when you are the author, you must be an accepted active member to turn listing on — owners and manage_storefront do not face that membership check. Coach tier. Needs the business:write scope.

**Reads or writes:** write · safe to repeat · **Plan:** Coach · **Scope:** `business:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `productId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `businessId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `storefrontListed` | boolean | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Per-binding discovery flag only — does not publish the business storefront master switch (use business_publish_storefront).
- Does not include the product in a tier or change membership pins; use include_tier_product for inclusions.
- Listing off blocks new storefront discovery for that binding; existing purchases and pinned inclusions stay entitled.

## `business_publish_storefront`

Publish or unpublish the customer-facing storefront for one of your provider businesses. Owner only: the database re-checks ownership under a lock on every call. Publishing makes the catalog visible for customer booking; unpublishing stops new holds but does not cancel existing bookings. Coach tier. Needs the business:write scope.

**Reads or writes:** write · safe to repeat · **Plan:** Coach · **Scope:** `business:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `businessId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `published` | boolean | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Unpublishing does not cancel confirmed or awaiting-payment bookings; it only blocks new public reads and bookings.
- This does not create checkout, capture payment, or grant any customer consent.

## `quote_provider_membership_checkout`

Read the authoritative monthly checkout quote for one published monthly tier of a provider business: the pinned tier version, the monthly amount and currency, the seller identity for confirmation (label SELLER — not a legal merchant-of-record claim), the opaque commercial-policy version id, and a quote fingerprint. Read-only: it reserves nothing, writes no consent and calls no payment provider. A later start_provider_membership_checkout revalidates everything against the reserve it pins. Personal tier. Needs the memberships:read scope.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `memberships:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tierId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Read-only: the quote reserves nothing and writes no consent; starting checkout revalidates every term against the reserve it pins.
- The quote fingerprint binds private commercial pins for consistency only — it is not authorization, and the private fee, plan and settlement terms it binds are never returned.
- Monthly membership checkout is disabled by default on this deployment (FYSIGO_PROVIDER_MEMBERSHIP_CHECKOUT_ENABLED unset): start_provider_membership_checkout refuses before any reserve, consent write or payment call while it is off. Existing memberships keep their paid-through access regardless.

## `start_provider_membership_checkout`

Start the caller's own monthly membership checkout for a published monthly tier, as a gated server actor: the core reserves the immutable terms, then a confirmation gate compares the human confirmation against the authoritative reserve and a fresh quote, recomputes the quote fingerprint from the server-side pins, records the standing train-at-your-own-risk acknowledgement once, and only then creates the Stripe-hosted checkout session. Requires BOTH the memberships:write and the opt-in memberships:payments scope, and an explicit human confirmation object that acknowledges the purchase and the risk and echoes the quote exactly (tier version, amountCents, currency, monthly recurrence, sellerProfileId, sellerDisplayName with role SELLER, businessId, policyVersionId, quoteFingerprint). Never charges the caller: returns a checkoutUrl (or a processing returnPath) for the human to finish on Stripe's own page. Personal tier.

**Reads or writes:** write · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `memberships:payments` + `memberships:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tierId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `locale` | `en` \| `es` | yes |  |
| `confirmation` | object | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Never charges the caller's card: a successful result is a Stripe-hosted checkout URL (or a processing returnPath) the human finishes in the browser; no auto-charge exists.
- Any confirmation mismatch refuses before any Stripe call or consent write, and the internal reserve stays pinned — call quote_provider_membership_checkout again and retry with a fresh confirmation of the new terms.
- The risk acknowledgement (train at your own risk) is recorded once, with this call's headers, only after every quoted term matches; no quote or mismatch ever writes consent.
- Seller is labelled SELLER for confirmation only — not a legal merchant-of-record claim. Private fee, plan and settlement terms are never returned in results, evidence or errors.
- Monthly membership checkout is disabled by default on this deployment (FYSIGO_PROVIDER_MEMBERSHIP_CHECKOUT_ENABLED unset) and refuses before any reserve, consent write or payment call while off.

## `cancel_provider_membership_billing`

Schedule cancellation of the caller's own billed monthly membership for one business at the end of the current paid period. Paid-through access is kept and the membership is not deleted immediately; the Stripe subscription is switched to cancel-at-period-end and the cancellation is recorded against the verified subscription. Requires BOTH the memberships:write and the opt-in memberships:payments scope, and the explicit literal confirmEndOfPeriod: true from the human. Works for existing billed memberships even while new checkout is disabled — it starts no new purchase. Personal tier.

**Reads or writes:** write · safe to repeat · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `memberships:payments` + `memberships:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `businessId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `confirmEndOfPeriod` | `true` | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Schedules cancellation at the end of the current paid period: accessUntil is the paid-through date that stays entitled, and nothing is deleted immediately.
- Needs an active billed monthly membership with a live, matching Stripe subscription; free memberships cancel with cancel_my_provider_membership instead.
- Works while new checkout is disabled (default off): it touches no new purchase and checks no checkout flag.
- The cancel-at-period-end schedule is confirmed on the Stripe subscription before the result reports cancelAtPeriodEnd; read get_my_provider_membership_billing_status afterwards for the recorded state.

## `get_my_provider_membership_billing_status`

Read the caller's own billing status for one provider business: whether a billed membership is active, canceled or absent, whether a checkout is pending, whether cancellation is scheduled at period end, and the paid-through date. This is the database's paid-through truth for the signed-in account only. Personal tier. Needs the memberships:read scope.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `memberships:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `businessId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Reads Fysigo's own records at call time — no webhook replay and no Stripe polling; a very recent Stripe change may not be reflected yet.
- A pending checkout can persist past its deadline while dispatch state is unknown: pendingCheckout true is not a completed purchase and not a charge.
- Never returns another profile's billing, purchase or payment metadata — only the signed-in account's own status for this business.

## `get_my_nutrition_today`

Your food log for one day (your time zone), as the app's Fuel Today does: macro targets and totals, pinned micronutrients with progress toward their targets, and every meal entry that day — each with its log id, meal slot, name, portion, time eaten (when recorded) and estimated energy. Today by default; pass date to read any other day, e.g. yesterday, to confirm what was eaten. Use the entry ids with update_my_food_log and delete_my_food_log (they work on any day), and read this again after log_my_food to confirm.

**Reads or writes:** read · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `nutrition:read`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | string | no | `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Reads one local day at a time (today unless date is given); for a range, read each day.
- timeOfDay is the local time the member said they ate, "HH:MM"; null when the entry was logged without a time, so an absent time is not evidence of when it was eaten.
- Totals combine your stored meal entries with the daily summary row when one exists; burnedKcal is null until a burn integration writes a value for the day.
- Energy on an entry is rounded from its stored nutrient snapshot; entries logged as estimates say so in confidence.

## `log_my_food`

Log what you ate: 1-10 items for one meal slot on one date (default: today in your time zone; past days are fine) at an optional time of day. Each item is either a catalog food (foodId from search_foods) or a rough staple (stapleSlug from list_food_staples) plus how many grams. Nutrient numbers are ALWAYS computed on the server from the food's per-100g values or the staple's averages — never send or invent nutrients. Returns the new log ids (use with delete_my_food_log) and each entry's estimated energy and protein. Read get_my_nutrition_today after an unclear result.

**Reads or writes:** write · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `nutrition:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mealName` | `breakfast` \| `lunch` \| `dinner` \| `snack` \| `pre_workout` \| `post_workout` | yes |  |
| `date` | string | no | `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` |
| `time` | string | no | `^([01]\d\|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d$` |
| `items` | array of any | yes |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Nutrients are estimates from per-100g catalog values or staple averages, not an analysis of the exact portion eaten.
- A staple entry is stored with confidence 'estimated'; a catalog food entry with 'verified'.
- time is optional and stored as the local wall-clock time; an entry logged without it simply has no time.
- After an unclear failure the save may still have landed: read get_my_nutrition_today (with the same date) before logging again.

## `update_my_food_log`

Edit one food entry you logged, as the app's editor does: fix the portion (grams per serving and/or number of servings), rename it, or move it to another meal slot, date or time of day. Send only what changes. Nutrient numbers are NEVER sent: the server re-scales the entry's stored nutrients by the new total grams (grams × quantity) over the old total, so halving the grams halves every nutrient, and the link to the catalog food is kept. A rename-only call changes just the name. Total eaten = grams × quantity, so for an entry logged with log_my_food (quantity 1) grams is the total. The log id is the entry id from get_my_nutrition_today; read it again afterwards to confirm the day's totals.

**Reads or writes:** write · safe to repeat · **Plan:** Personal or Coach · **Scope:** `nutrition:write`

| Argument | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `logId` | string (uuid) | yes |  |
| `grams` | number | no |  |
| `quantity` | number | no |  |
| `displayName` | string | no |  |
| `mealName` | `breakfast` \| `lunch` \| `dinner` \| `snack` \| `pre_workout` \| `post_workout` | no |  |
| `mealDate` | string | no | `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$` |
| `timeOfDay` | any | no |  |

**What a result cannot tell you**

- Nutrients are scaled in proportion to the portion from the values stored when the entry was logged; renaming an entry does not change its nutrients, so a differently prepared food (soft-boiled vs raw) keeps the original food's nutrient profile.
- Rounding to two decimals means editing the portion up and back down may drift a nutrient by a hundredth.
